name: Thinkster Math
line: Thinkster pairs AI practice with a weekly tutor. AMP shows worked steps every time, for $59 a month.
description: AMP vs Thinkster Math: weekly tutoring from $22.50 a session with an AI coach, or adaptive practice from counting to precalculus for $59 a month.
verdict: Thinkster Math gives a learner the same tutor every week and an AI coach at any hour, and that is worth something [1][2]. Its lowest listed price, $22.50 a session, comes to about $97.50 a month at one session a week (our arithmetic) [2]; AMP is $59 a month. AMP shows the worked answer after every problem, keeps a mastery rule anyone can read, and brings old skills back on a schedule.
theirs: Thinkster Math is an online math tutoring service sold to families at hellothinkster.com. Its home page sums it up as tutoring personalized by patented AI and top math tutors [1]. Two plans share one system. Ignite pairs a learner with a certified dedicated tutor; Signature pairs them with a masters-certified tutor, with SPED options and a money-back guarantee [2]. Both include live 45-minute one-to-one sessions, one to three times a week, a 24/7 AI coach, a mastery map and a parent dashboard [2].

A trial starts with a 7-minute assessment that maps the learner's skills and gaps, then a free one-to-one session with a tutor [1]. Day to day, the learner spends 15 to 20 minutes, five days a week, on targeted practice that Thinkster's AI creates [1]. Each worksheet comes with a video tutorial, and the mastery map updates after every worksheet [1]. Tutors leave feedback on worksheets, and in each session the tutor reviews the learner's week of work [1]. The AI coach answers at any hour with Socratic prompts and does not give the answer [1][2].

Thinkster's tutoring covers K-8 math, Algebra 1 and Geometry, aligned to Common Core and state standards [1][2]. Learners who practice consistently earn a $5 gift card each month [1]. The site also offers free printable worksheets by grade and topic [3].
credit: A real person. The same dedicated tutor every session, in live 45-minute one-to-one sessions up to three times a week; Signature tutors are masters-certified, with SPED options [1][2]. AMP has no tutors.
An AI coach at any hour, for homework help too, that guides with Socratic prompts rather than giving the answer [1][2]. AMP has no AI tutor.

An engine built to read how a learner got a problem wrong. Thinkster says it tells a slip in calculation from a wrong idea and adjusts difficulty at every problem [1]. AMP checks typed lines of work on 64 problem types, not freehand work.
Rewards for steady practice: a $5 gift card each month [1]. AMP has no games or reward store.

reasons.title: A month of AMP costs less than three sessions
reasons.body: Thinkster's tutoring plans start at $22.50 a session for Ignite and $45 for Signature in K-8, with one to three live sessions a week [2]. At the lowest listed price, one session a week comes to about $97.50 a month (our arithmetic: $22.50 x 52 weeks / 12). AMP is $59 a month or $599 a year, with no session fees, however much the learner practices. Two parents practice free on the same plan.

reasons.title: Mastery is a rule anyone can read
reasons.body: Thinkster's mastery map colors each skill green for mastered, yellow for in progress and red for needs attention, and updates after every worksheet [1]. Its pages do not say what earns green [1][2]. In AMP a skill is Strong when four of the last five answers are right without help. An answer given after a hint or the lesson does not count, two misses in a row send practice back to what the skill builds on, and the rule is in AMP's public source code.

reasons.title: The worked answer arrives with every answer
reasons.body: At Thinkster, help comes from an AI coach that guides a stuck learner with Socratic prompts and never gives the answer, and from tutor feedback on worksheets that the learner reviews [1]. AMP shows, at every answer, right or wrong, the correct answer and the worked steps; its one-step hint also never gives the answer away. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, feedback that explains averaged 0.49, the correct answer alone 0.32, and right-or-wrong only 0.05 [9].

reasons.title: Old skills come back on a schedule
reasons.body: Thinkster says its engine traces a gap back through the concepts underneath it and rebuilds from there [1]; its pages describe no schedule for revisiting skills already mastered [1][2]. AMP repairs prerequisites too, and it also brings each learned skill back after 6 hours, 1 day, 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks and a month, mixed with other topics; a miss restarts the schedule. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' own test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [8].

reasons.title: One program from counting to precalculus
reasons.body: Thinkster's tutoring covers K-8 math, Algebra 1 and Geometry, and the Algebra 1 and Geometry band has its own prices: $25 a session for Ignite and $59.50 for Signature [2]. AMP covers counting through precalculus, 336 skills on one prerequisite map, at one price. Any learner can work in any band, Algebra 2 and precalculus included.

reasons.title: Paper practice made for each learner
reasons.body: Thinkster offers free printable worksheets, sorted by grade and topic, for at-home practice [3]. AMP prints unlimited workbooks built from each learner's own answers, with review of the skills that are due and a worked answer key. Results entered from paper count toward the learner's level.

rows.buyers: Families, through plans sold on its website, billed monthly, quarterly or annually [2].
rows.range: K-8 math, Algebra 1 and Geometry [2]. Aligned to Common Core and state standards [1].

rows.evidence: No entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse as of November 2026 [4][5]. No outcome study found.

theirs: We found no published outcome study of Thinkster Math, randomized or with a comparison group. It has no entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse as of November 2026 [4][5]. Its home page lists figures such as 3x faster learning and 18+ months gained in 6 months, beside individual families' test reports, without naming a study behind them [1].

In place of a study, Thinkster offers a guarantee: a full refund if a learner shows no "measurable improvement" after six months of consistent engagement [1]. The family must meet six standards, among them 10 worksheets a week, 80% of assigned videos watched and 90% of sessions attended, and progress is tracked on Thinkster's own mastery map [1][2]. In our view a guarantee is a business term, not evidence of learning.

Tutoring as a method has strong research behind it. Across 263 randomized trials, tutoring averaged 0.40 standard deviations; for large U.S. programs measured on standardized tests the figure was 0.16 to 0.22 [6]. Effects tended to be larger at three or more days a week [7]. Those trials did not test Thinkster, whose plans offer one to three sessions a week [2].
ours: AMP's rules come from findings that have held up in trials. Worked examples improved math performance by an average of g = 0.48 across 55 studies [10], and AMP shows worked steps after every answer. Mixed, spaced practice scored 62% against 38% a month later on the researchers' own test, in a randomized trial that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations [8], and AMP schedules that review for every learned skill. We think that, for a learner who needs practice more than conversation, a program that does this at every problem, most days, is a better buy than a weekly session. That is our bet, and we have committed to testing it in public.

AMP is new, and its own outcome studies have not run yet. They begin in 2027: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. Until then, the research behind each part of AMP is laid out in our report, and the code is public.

them: Your child does best with the same tutor, every week [1].
You want a tutor and an AI coach for help with school homework [1].
You want live sessions up to three times a week [2].
Your child is motivated by a monthly reward for steady practice [1].
amp: You want daily practice for less than three tutor sessions a month.
You want the worked answer shown after every problem.
You want old skills to come back on a schedule, without planning it.
You want one program from counting through precalculus.
You already pay a tutor and want daily practice between sessions.

questions.question: How much does Thinkster Math cost compared with AMP?
questions.answer: Thinkster's tutoring starts at $22.50 a session for Ignite and $45 for Signature in K-8, and at $25 and $59.50 for Algebra 1 and Geometry, with one to three sessions a week [2]. AMP is $599 a year or $59 a month for the first child and $399 or $39 for each more, with a full refund within 30 days.

questions.question: Does Thinkster Math guarantee results?
questions.answer: It refunds in full if a learner shows no measurable improvement after six months, when the family meets six engagement standards; progress is tracked on its own mastery map [1][2]. AMP refunds any personal payment within 30 days with no reason needed. It does not promise a learning result.

questions.question: Can AMP replace a Thinkster tutor?
questions.answer: Not as a person. AMP has no tutors and no AI tutor. It places the learner, chooses and checks every problem, and schedules review, and many families can use it between sessions with any tutor.

questions.question: What grades does Thinkster Math cover?
questions.answer: Its tutoring covers K-8 math, Algebra 1 and Geometry [2]. AMP covers counting through precalculus in one program, at one price.
